gloss: to relocate; to move; to transfer

definitions.gloss: to relocate; to move (a business, office, etc.)
definitions.explanation: To move the location of an organization, business, or residence to a new place.
To transfer legal rights, ownership, or registration from one party to another.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}が{移転|いてん}した。
{来月|らいげつ}、オフィスが{駅前|えきまえ}に{移転|いてん}する。
examples.english: The office is relocating in front of the station next month.

examples.japanese: {老朽化|ろうきゅうか}した{工場|こうじょう}を{郊外|こうがい}の{新|あたら}しい{場所|ばしょ}に{移転|いてん}することが{決|き}まった。
examples.english: It was decided to relocate the aging factory to a new location in the suburbs.

examples.japanese: {所有権|しょゆうけん}を{移転|いてん}する。
{不動産|ふどうさん}の{登記|とうき}を{移転|いてん}した。
examples.english: I transferred the real estate registration.

examples.japanese: {相続|そうぞく}によって{土地|とち}の{所有権|しょゆうけん}が{子|こ}どもに{移転|いてん}された。
examples.english: Ownership of the land was transferred to the children through inheritance.

notes:
Used for formal or official moves — businesses, offices, government agencies. Not typically used for individuals moving house (use {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す instead). Also a key legal term for transfer of rights.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事務所|じむしょ}を{移転|いてん}する: to relocate an office
- {本社|ほんしゃ}{移転|いてん}: headquarters relocation
- {所有権|しょゆうけん}{移転|いてん}: transfer of ownership
- {移転|いてん}{先|さき}: new location (after relocation)
- {移転|いてん}{費用|ひよう}: relocation costs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す: to move (house) — for personal/household moves
- {転居|てんきょ}する: to change residence — formal term for personal moves
- {譲渡|じょうと}する: to transfer, to assign — specifically for rights or assets
